findings.highlight: under the impression that I'm here to help on a rainy day
findings.evidenceJa: ただ『地獄に仏』とばかりに、早く制服に着替えるよう、更衣室を指差してくれるかもしれない。
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines the short-staffed restaurant welcoming his unexpected arrival like a Buddha appearing in hell—that is, as a godsend in desperate circumstances. The English invents helping on a rainy day, an unrelated situation that obscures why the staff would immediately send him to change into uniform.
findings.japanese:
唐突に訪れた俺のことを奇異に思わず、
ただ『地獄に仏』とばかりに、早く制服に着替えるよう、
更衣室を指差してくれるかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: My abrupt visit might instinctively strike them as unusual, but they'd probably direct me to the changing room and put me into uniform under the impression that I'm here to help on a rainy day.

findings.highlight: In terms of your mental state, that is!
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩はよくてもわたしがよくないんです！精神衛生上！
findings.explanation: Koharu says that even if Haruki is content to leave, she is not, because abandoning him would be bad for her own peace of mind. The English instead comments on Haruki's mental state, removing Koharu's explicit reason for chasing and caring for him.
findings.japanese:
「先輩はよくてもわたしがよくないんです！
精神衛生上！」
findings.todokanai: "You might think you're alright, but to me, you're not! In terms of your mental state, that is!"

findings.highlight: I'd have to tell her everything
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は全てを知ろうとするだろう。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that Koharu would actively try to learn everything in exchange for giving him comfort. The English turns that into an obligation for Haruki to tell her everything, changing Koharu's interventionist agency.
findings.japanese:
けれど俺が心の安らぎを得るのと引き替えに、
彼女は全てを知ろうとするだろう。
findings.todokanai: In exchange for getting peace of mind, however, I'd have to tell her everything.

findings.highlight: She was desperately chasing after me… and in the end, she caught up to me.
findings.evidenceJa: 必死で、俺を追いかけてきてくれ…追いかけてきた。
findings.explanation: Haruki begins to think Koharu 'came after me for my sake' and then corrects himself to the neutral 'came after me'; the English changes this to chased and caught up.
findings.japanese: 必死で、俺を追いかけてきてくれ…追いかけてきた。
findings.todokanai: She was desperately chasing after me… and in the end, she caught up to me.

findings.evidenceJa: アオムシで鯨を釣りやがって…
findings.explanation: Haruki jokes that the manager has caught a whale with a caterpillar: by forgiving one short absence, he has secured Koharu's labor beyond April. Calling this merely a rip-off deletes both sides of the deliberately absurd bait-versus-catch image and the joke about the manager's enormous return.
findings.japanese: アオムシで鯨を釣りやがって…

findings.highlight: she's not a fan of warm beverages
findings.evidenceJa: 甘党じゃない代わりに猫舌だったか。
findings.explanation: 猫舌 means that Koharu is sensitive to food or drink being too hot, as her blowing on the canned coffee demonstrates. The English instead says she dislikes warm beverages, inventing a preference and missing the physical trait behind the beat.
findings.japanese: 甘党じゃない代わりに猫舌だったか。
findings.todokanai: It seems she's not a fan of warm beverages despite lacking a sweet tooth.

findings.highlight: you seem to be so serious all the time
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦は…どんな時にでもまっすぐ来るよな。いい意味でも、悪い意味でも
findings.explanation: Haruki says Koharu always comes at things straight, for better or worse. She answers that Haruki is always twisted or contrary. The English makes her merely serious and, in the next line, him depressed, destroying the paired straight-versus-crooked characterization on which the exchange turns.
findings.japanese:
「杉浦は…どんな時にでもまっすぐ来るよな。
いい意味でも、悪い意味でも」
findings.todokanai: "You know… for better or worse, you seem to be so serious all the time, Sugiura."

findings.highlight: unhindered by the usual possibility of me giving a light retort and potentially causing the conversation to go nowhere
findings.evidenceJa: いつもみたいに軽く切り返せずに会話を詰まらせてしまう俺を、自分が話し続けることにより受け止めてくれてた。
findings.explanation: Haruki is the one unable to make his usual light rejoinders, so he lets the conversation stall; Koharu carries and accepts him by continuing to speak herself. The English says his usual rejoinders might cause the conversation to fail and portrays Koharu as simply unhindered, reversing the immediate conversational mechanics and obscuring her tact.
findings.japanese:
いつもみたいに軽く切り返せずに
会話を詰まらせてしまう俺を、
自分が話し続けることにより受け止めてくれてた。
findings.todokanai: She continues talking about her own life without stopping, unhindered by the usual possibility of me giving a light retort and potentially causing the conversation to go nowhere because of it.

findings.highlight: She went from directly intervening to influencing from the sidelines
findings.evidenceJa: 介入し続けるお節介から、介入しないことで焼くお節介に。
findings.explanation: Haruki contrasts her former meddling by continual intervention with a new kind of meddling expressed precisely by not intervening. 'Influencing from the sidelines' removes the paradoxical non-intervention and therefore the evidence of how Koharu's care has matured.
findings.japanese:
介入し続けるお節介から、
介入しないことで焼くお節介に。
findings.todokanai: She went from directly intervening to influencing from the sidelines.

findings.highlight: So it's not that "she's become a companion for me to talk to," but rather "she wants to be a companion for me to talk to," is it…
findings.evidenceJa: 『話し相手になってあげる』じゃなくて『話し相手になってもらう』か…
findings.explanation: Haruki notices that Koharu said not 'I'll be your conversation partner' but 'I'll have you be mine': she frames the company as something she receives from him, making her need reciprocal rather than patronizing. Both English clauses make Koharu the companion for Haruki, so the explicitly quoted grammatical distinction disappears.
findings.japanese:
『話し相手になってあげる』じゃなくて
『話し相手になってもらう』か…
findings.todokanai: So it's not that "she's become a companion for me to talk to," but rather "she wants to be a companion for me to talk to," is it…

findings.highlight: I can't force you two to date each other
findings.evidenceJa: 付き合えないのはしょうがないけれど、それでも先輩は彼女の憧れだったんです
findings.explanation: Koharu accepts that Haruki cannot date Mihoko, then reminds him that he was still the person Mihoko admired. The English changes this into Koharu's inability to force them together, relocating the constraint from Haruki's relationship decision to Koharu's influence.
findings.japanese:
「付き合えないのはしょうがないけれど、
それでも先輩は彼女の憧れだったんです」
findings.todokanai: "I can't force you two to date each other, but she still looks up to you."

findings.highlight: I want her to properly accept that
findings.evidenceJa: そのことはちゃんと受け止めて欲しいし、友達に戻って欲しいと思ってる
findings.explanation: Koharu wants Haruki, the person she is addressing, to acknowledge what Mihoko's admiration meant and to become her friend again. The English says Mihoko should accept it, reversing who Koharu is asking to face the emotional fact.
findings.japanese:
「そのことはちゃんと受け止めて欲しいし、
友達に戻って欲しいと思ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I want her to properly accept that and for the two of you to go back to being friends again."

findings.evidenceJa: いつもの何倍も魅力的に…そして、いつも通りの頼もしい存在に映った。
findings.explanation: Koharu appears many times more attractive than usual yet as reliable as ever. The English makes both qualities increase, deleting the point that her new attractiveness coexists with the familiar dependability Haruki already trusted.
findings.japanese:
彼女は、いつもの何倍も魅力的に…
そして、いつも通りの頼もしい存在に映った。
findings.todokanai: She appears to be even much more attractive than usual… and even more reliable as well.

findings.highlight: hold onto it without offering any resistance
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦の差し出した手を、何のてらいもなく握ることしかできなかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki takes Koharu's offered hand without self-consciousness or affected hesitation. The English says he offers no resistance, recasting his simple active acceptance as passive submission and changing the agency of the intimate gesture.
findings.japanese:
だから、杉浦の差し出した手を、
何のてらいもなく握ることしかできなかった。
findings.todokanai: That's why when Sugiura offered her hand, I couldn't do anything but hold onto it without offering any resistance.
